name: StatusType
summary: Makes planned and actual a type object an observation names, so that a plan's figures and the world's figures are the same kind of thing and can be compared without a special case.

roles.name: StatusType
roles.summary: The status as a type object, so that which statuses exist is configured rather than written as classes. The alternative — a subclass per status, or a boolean — makes comparing a plan against an outcome a special case instead of an ordinary observation.

roles.name: Actual
roles.summary: A status asserting the observation is of the world as it was. It may carry a time offset, so that a figure stated a month after the period it covers is distinguished from the same figure restated later.

roles.name: Planned
roles.summary: A status asserting the observation belongs to a plan, and naming which. Two plans for one period are therefore two sets of observations rather than two columns on one.

roles.name: Plan
roles.summary: The plan a planned status refers to. Making it an object rather than a label is what lets one plan's observations be gathered, and what lets a plan be superseded without rewriting the figures it held.

roles.name: ComparativeStatusType
roles.summary: A status type whose observations compare a datum against a comparator — a variance. It is a status rather than a calculation because what it yields is an observation like any other, and so can itself be planned or actual.

roles.name: Status
roles.summary: The status type an observation names. One reference, on the observation rather than on its subtype, is what makes planned and actual interchangeable to everything that reads observations.
